entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0371: `zbus_names` is unmaintained
entry.content:
`zbus_names` is unmaintained

Affected:

  • zbus_names

The `zbus_names` crate is no longer maintained as a standalone crate. It has been merged into [`zbus`](https://crates.io/crates/zbus) starting with version `6.0.0`, as its `names` module. Users should migrate to [`zbus`](https://crates.io/crates/zbus), with its default features disabled if they only need the D-Bus name types.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zbus_names
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0371.html
  • https://github.com/z-galaxy/zbus/issues/2043

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0373: Missing case-insensitive matching for CSS url function
entry.content:
Missing case-insensitive matching for CSS url function

Aliases: GHSA-x43w-36pp-96g3

Affected:

  • ammonia — fixed in 4.1.8, 4.2.4

URL filtering, such as relative URLs and URL scheme limits, is not always applied when CSS sanitization is used. When the inner URL is quoted, CSS `url("")` is matched case-sensitively, when it should be matched case-insensitively. As a result, while `url("")` gets the intended domain name filtering, `URL("")` does not. The following example shows how an application needs to be configured to trigger this bug. ```rust let mut builder = Builder::new(); // allow inline styles builder.filter_style_properties(hashset!["background-image"]); builder.add_generic_attributes(&["style"]); // notice that "http" URLs aren't allowed builder.url_schemes(["cid"].into()); // attacker-controlled, presumably let cleaned = builder.clean(r#"<div style='background:URL("https://evil.com/ping");'>"#); // thi…

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/ammonia
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0373.html
  • https://github.com/rust-ammonia/ammonia/pull/267

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-6fj4-rcr3-r7rr: lopdf has a stack overflow via deeply nested PDF objects
entry.content:
lopdf has a stack overflow via deeply nested PDF objects

Aliases: RUSTSEC-2026-0187

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • lopdf — fixed in 0.42.0

`lopdf::Document::load_mem` (and the other `load*` entry points) parses nested PDF arrays and dictionaries with unbounded recursion. A small crafted PDF whose Catalog contains a deeply nested array (`/X [[[ … ]]]`, on the order of 10,000 levels) exhausts the call stack and aborts the process with `SIGABRT`. Because this is a stack-overflow abort rather than a `panic!`, it cannot be caught with `catch_unwind`: any service that parses untrusted PDF input with lopdf can be crashed by a ~21 KB file, resulting in a denial of service. Confirmed on lopdf 0.41.0 and earlier; fixed in 0.42.0. entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0367: Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation
entry.content:
Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation

Aliases: GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • zip — fixed in 9.0.0

The `zip` crate preserves privileged Unix permission bits (SUID, SGID, and sticky bits) from ZIP `external_attributes` during extraction, instead of masking them to safe permission bits. If a privileged process (for example, `root` in an installer, CI/CD pipeline, or container build) extracts an attacker-controlled ZIP archive using `ZipArchive::extract()` or the stream extraction API, files can be created as setuid-root or setgid. This behavior allows the creation of SUID/SGID files during extraction, which can lead to local privilege escalation depending on the execution environment. For further details see: https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zip
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0367.html

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0366: Stack overflow when parsing deeply nested input in pest_grammars
entry.content:
Stack overflow when parsing deeply nested input in pest_grammars

Aliases: GHSA-7632-4q2x-hvjw

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • pest_grammars — fixed in 2.9.3

## Impact In affected versions, parsing deeply nested input with `pest_grammars::json::JsonParser` can exhaust the native stack and abort the hosting process. Applications that accept attacker-controlled JSON without suitable resource limits may therefore be vulnerable to denial of service. The reported reproduction demonstrates this behavior with deeply nested JSON arrays. The nesting required to trigger an overflow depends on the platform, available stack space, and build configuration; there is no portable safe nesting threshold. ## Patches Upgrade to `pest_grammars` 2.9.3 or later. Version 2.9.3 requires the updated `pest` runtime and includes regression tests for deeply nested JSON with the optional call budget disabled. Supported std builds automatically check available native s…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0368: zip: `ZipArchive::extract` creates symbolic links whose attacker-controlled targets are outside the destination directory
entry.content:
zip: `ZipArchive::extract` creates symbolic links whose attacker-controlled targets are outside the destination directory

Aliases: GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26

Affected:

  • zip — fixed in 9.0.0

In `zip` 9.0.0-pre2, `ZipArchive::extract` creates a symbolic link from an archive entry after validating only the output entry path. The link target bytes are passed directly to the platform symlink API, so a malicious archive can create an entry inside the destination that resolves to an attacker-chosen path outside it. This behavior was verified on macOS and Linux. On either platform, a subsequent application read or write through that extracted entry accesses the external target with the extracting process's permissions. For further details see: https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zip
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0368.html

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0365: Remote DoS through unchecked `IdList` allocation in negentropy
entry.content:
Remote DoS through unchecked `IdList` allocation in negentropy

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • negentropy — fixed in 0.4.4, 0.5.2

## Summary The `negentropy` crate is vulnerable to denial-of-service through an unchecked, peer-controlled ID count in reconciliation messages. With the `std` feature enabled, which is the default configuration, a small malformed message can trigger an enormous memory allocation and terminate the application. ## Details When processing an `IdList` range, the reconciliation parser uses the peer-provided ID count to reserve memory before checking whether the message contains the corresponding IDs: ```rust let mut their_elems: HashSet<Id> = HashSet::with_capacity(num_ids as usize); ``` An attacker can declare an arbitrarily large count without supplying any IDs. The allocation occurs before the parser reaches the ID-reading loop, which would otherwise reject the truncated message. …

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-4ch3-9j33-3pmj: Wasmtime: WASI hard links bypass wasmtime-wasi's FilePerms for destination
entry.content:
Wasmtime: WASI hard links bypass wasmtime-wasi's FilePerms for destination

Aliases: CVE-2026-58494, RUSTSEC-2026-0188

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • wasmtime-wasi — fixed in 24.0.11
  • wasmtime-wasi — fixed in 36.0.12
  • wasmtime-wasi — fixed in 45.0.3
  • wasmtime-wasi — fixed in 46.0.1

## Summary Wasmtime's WASI filesystem implementation lets a guest with a read-only source file capability overwrite that file by hard-linking it into another preopen that allows file writes. An attacker who can run a WASI guest can bypass `WasiCtxBuilder` per-preopen `FilePerms` and modify host files that were exposed as `FilePerms::READ`. This attack is possible through the wasip1, wasip2, and wasip3 interfaces to the WASI filesystem. This attack is also possible through an indirection of renaming a hardlink into another preopen. ### Details `WasiCtxBuilder::preopened_dir` documents `file_perms` as the maximum permissions usable for files in that preopen. However, hard-link creation and renaming only checked directory mutation for permission, and not whether the file permissions matc…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2cv4-cqwr-gwf7: uv: Path traversal on Windows through wheel extraction
entry.content:
uv: Path traversal on Windows through wheel extraction

Aliases: CVE-2026-104843, PYSEC-2026-4305

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • uv — fixed in 0.12.18
  • uv — fixed in 0.12.18

### Impact In versions of uv from 0.12.7 to 0.12.18 on Windows, uv could be induced into writing a file outside of the installation prefix during wheel installation. A malicious wheel could use this to place an executable outside of the intended environment, including in a directory already present on the user's PATH. This vulnerability only affects Windows hosts; no other platforms are affected. ### Patches uv 0.12.18 and newer address this vulnerability. Users are encouraged to upgrade to 0.12.18. ### Workarounds There is no workaround other than upgrading to uv 0.12.18.
